source.label: Wikipedia: “one of the earliest and most emblematic works of his Tahitian period”
Wikipedia: in Tahiti he “sought what he imagined to be an untouched, ‘primitive’ world”

highlight.text: I am leaving in order to have peace and quiet, to be rid of the influence of civilization. I want only to do simple, very simple art … to render, the way a child would, the concepts formed in my brain
highlight.lead: Telling a Paris journalist why he was going to Tahiti, 1891:

source.author: Paul Gauguin
source.title: Interview with Jules Huret, L'Écho de Paris, 23 February 1891, in The Writings of a Savage (1996), p. 48, quoted on Wikiquote
source.license: Short excerpt of an English translation, via Wikiquote (CC BY-SA)

source.label: Wikipedia: Ia Orana Maria, oil on canvas

work.text: I have done one picture: An angel with yellow wings points out a Tahitian Mary and Jesus to two native women—nudes clothed with a pareo, a sort of flowered cotton cloth, that can be attached as one likes to the waist. … The road dark violet, the foreground emerald green.
work.lead: Writing to his friend Daniel de Monfreid:

source.author: Paul Gauguin
source.title: Letter to Georges-Daniel de Monfreid, Tahiti, 11 March 1892
source.publisher: The Letters of Paul Gauguin to Georges Daniel de Monfreid, trans. Ruth Pielkovo (Dodd, Mead, 1922), Internet Archive scan

work.text: Although Gauguin explored themes of Catholic theology in his art during his second stay in the South Seas, [Ia Orana Maria] is the only explicitly Christian painting from his first trip to Tahiti.

moment.text: Further off, a stained-glass window full of richly-coloured flowers, human flowers and flowers of plants; with her divine child on her shoulder, an aureoled apparition of a woman, before whom two others clasp hands amid the blossoms, with the gestures of a seraph
moment.lead: The critic Achille Delaroche, evoking the picture in an essay Gauguin kept:

source.author: Achille Delaroche
source.title: “Concerning the Painter Paul Gauguin, from an Aesthetic Point of View”, reprinted in Paul Gauguin's Intimate Journals
source.publisher: Paul Gauguin's Intimate Journals, trans. Van Wyck Brooks (1923), Internet Archive scan

moment.text: In addition to Tahitian influence, Gauguin drew inspiration from the relief sculpture of Borobudur, the 9th-century Buddhist temple in Java of which Gauguin owned photographs.

matters.text: Life at Papeete soon became a burden. It was Europe — the Europe which I had thought to shake off … Was I to have made this far journey, only to find the very thing which I had fled?
matters.lead: On arriving in the colonial capital, as told in Noa Noa:

source.author: Paul Gauguin
source.title: Noa Noa, trans. O. F. Theis

matters.text: Following its 1893 exhibition in Paris, [Ia Orana Maria] was one of the few works Gauguin managed to sell. The 2,000 francs he received was the highest price of any work he had sold up to that date.
